class.name: LuaTable
class.brief_description: A Lua table object that allows interaction with Lua tables from GDScript.
class.description: The LuaTable class provides methods to manipulate Lua tables, including getting/setting values, converting to Godot arrays and dictionaries, and iterating over table contents.

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes all elements from the table.

method.name: get_value
method.description:
Returns the value associated with the given key. May invoke metatable's [code]__index[/code] method if key is not present in the table. If no value is associated with key, returns the specified default value. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var table = lua_state.create_table({ "foo": "bar", "baz": 42 }) var value = table.get_value("foo") print(value) # Prints "bar"
# String keys also support `get` method, [] operator or `.` notation value = table.get("foo") or table["foo"] or table.foo print(value) # Prints "bar" [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]

method.name: length
method.description: Returns the length of the array part of the table. This matches Lua's # operator behavior and calls the [code]__len[/code] metamethod if present. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var lua = LuaState.new() var table: LuaTable = lua.do_string(""" local table = { [1] = "A", [2] = "B", name = "Table", [3] = "C", [5] = "E", lv = 12 } return table """) print(table.length()) # Prints 3 [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]

method.name: rawget
method.description: Returns the value associated with the given key without invoking metatable's [code]__index[/code] method.

method.name: rawset
method.description: Sets the value for the given key without invoking metatable's [code]__newindex[/code] method.

method.name: set_metatable
method.description: Set a new metatable for this table. See [url]https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#2.4[/url]

method.name: set_value
method.description:
Sets the value for the given key. May invoke metatable's [code]__newindex[/code] method if key is not present in the table. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var table = lua_state.create_table({ "foo": "bar", "baz": 42 }) # Using set method table.set_value("foo", "baz") print(table.get_value("foo")) # Prints "baz"
# String keys also support `set` method, [] operator or `.` notation table.set("foo", "baz") table["foo"] = "baz" table.foo = baz print(table.get_value("foo")) # Prints "baz" [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]

method.name: to_array
to_dictionary
